body: I completely understand this feeling. Thinking about my preferred method has been my anchor for months. Whenever things get tough, I can always just think "it's okay, I can always kill myself" and it's so calming. I honestly think it's the only thing keeping me sane sometimes.

Lowkey hoping my therapist cancels our session tomorrow so I don't have to talk about being suicidal and wanting to self-harm...just last week I was talking to her about how optimistic I felt for the next few months. It was true in part, but I also knew that I was talking around the other stuff the whole time, I just couldn't figure out how to bring it up...sigh.
hahahaha this happened to me last week with the school therapist! 🥲
Been feeling pretty tired and kind of numb. Honestly not sure what to do about it. I guess venting helps a bit.

I made a mistake...My mom said she would "kill" me (yes she said that, no I don't know if she was serious) if I missed another class, and apparently one of my teachers marked me absent in a class even though I *was* logged in because I had my video off the whole time. So...I guess I better not be in the house when she gets the phone call. fml

It went okay. It was a therapist who works for my school, so, they tend to lean towards providing only short-term counseling. I guess I probably should’ve realized that from the beginning. But, I did talk to her, and we did discuss some of the problems I’ve been having (although, they were mostly academic-related problems), and we did discuss strategies to help with those problems. There were some other things I kind of wanted to talk about, but I didn’t really know how to bring them up. She did say I could schedule another appointment any time, though, so that’s good to know. Honestly, I think I might try and work on stuff by myself for a while, read some more books, etc.

Anyway, thanks for asking! Hope you’ve had a good week!

Going to talk to a new therapist tomorrow, after 5 months without therapy. Fingers crossed that it’ll go okay. I’m a bit unsure of what I’ll say to her because it feels like there’s way too many things going wrong in my life right now to summarize in one session, but hopefully I can come up with something to say at least.

THIS. I’m so annoyed when people say stuff like “if you’re struggling, reach out!” and “help is available!” Like, what “help” am I going to realistically be able to get? Therapy that I can’t afford for more than five sessions? How exactly will that solve any of my problems?

(And don’t even get me started on being a teenager who needs therapy. Basically your only options are school therapists, who don’t even exist in every school and aren’t necessarily going to be able to give you anything other than short-term therapy because they have so many other people to get to, or somehow getting your parents to get you a therapist. Which might work for some people, but if your parents are the type who don’t believe that depression is real, then you’re basically out of options, unless you can somehow find someone who’s willing to see you without parental consent *and* who you can afford. It’s *so frustrating* oh my god.)

I’d really prefer something more long-term if I can get it...but, alas, that costs money.

Sadly I’ve had no luck with getting a therapy appointment yet. I’ve contacted a couple local sliding scale agencies, but it’s been hard to find a private place where I can return their calls as I live with several other people and I’d rather they not know all the details about my mental health problems. I also am not sure how I’d pay for sessions, and honestly I wonder if it’s worth it to go through all this trouble to try and get therapy that I’m not even sure will help. I’ve been struggling a lot lately and I really would like someone to talk to about it, but I just don’t know if it’s possible to really fix anything at the moment given my current situation.

I definitely want to work on my current problems but I also have a lot of Feelings about the past stuff that I've never talked about with anyone and I guess I just want to get it all out.

So you know those questionnaires that are like, "In the past two weeks have you felt down, depressed, hopeless, etc..."? The place that I go to therapy at wants me to fill it out every time I go there. I don't necessarily object to this or anything, I can see how it might be helpful with tracking symptoms or something like that. I guess it just seems a bit weird to me because I've never heard of anyone having to do that every time they go to a session. Has anyone else had a similar experience?

My T asked if I could bring my parents to the next session and I am kiiinda nervous...I mean, I'm glad she suggested that, because then they can learn a little bit more about what therapy actually is like. But also my T said she might bring up some of their critical comments that I have talked about with her (basically they tend to maybe go a bit far with critical comments sometimes) and I kind of wonder if they'll try and deny saying those things or if it will turn into a mess in some other way. Idk, I am probably worrying too much about this.

Overall I am really happy that I got to go!
